correctness.rationale: For an edge differing in coordinate i, the number of common neighbors is exactly q_i-2. Thus formulas with three variables define the binary and nonbinary coordinate edges. For any two anchors, the support of a third vertex's four colored distances is the direct product of coordinate-local choices; these local choices depend only on counts of binary and nonbinary matching and differing coordinates. Maintaining both colored pair distances gives Duplicator an indefinitely reusable three-pebble winning strategy. Conversely, three-variable formulas express finite B- and N-path distances exactly k (with alpha-renaming in the definable edges), recovering binary and nonbinary dimensions. Representatives and FO2/FO4 boundaries follow. Independently enumerated coordinate-extension support agrees on 5,670 ordered anchor pairs in 15 graphs and stabilized 3-variable logical refinement agrees on 12 inter-graph comparisons; these are finite corroborations, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Prior full texts and available research claims were compared at the level of implication. Mixed-factor graph embedding characterizations, generic pebble-game theorems, earlier uniform-distance-regular FO3 support theorems, and fixed-quantifier-rank rook-graph studies do not directly entail the complete unrestricted-FO3 classification for mixed Cartesian clique products, which are generally not distance-regular. No equivalent result was identified among inspected sources and actual database searches; historical-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: A broader unindexed algebraic model-theory theorem for Cartesian graph products or finite variable relational reducts could imply the classification; no global historical novelty certification is claimed.
The prior general distance-regular support result covers uniform Hamming cases, so the material new scope is mixed factors, their definable edge categories, and sharp combined invariants.

value.rationale: Complete and exact classification of an infinite natural graph family under unrestricted-depth finite-variable noncounting logic, extending beyond uniform distance-regular Hamming graphs to all mixed alphabet sizes. The binary/nonbinary coordinate split is an intrinsic definable invariant, each d-factor family has exactly d+1 theories, the representatives of orders 2^b 3^s are minimal, and a 3-vs-4 variable boundary demonstrates a genuine expressive-power limitation. These are structurally motivated rather than arbitrary finite computations.
